primary_meaning: When “east” is given a positive symbolic meaning in Christian interpretation, it most commonly represents the manifestation or coming of God—especially Christ’s return—and, by association, light, resurrection, and paradise. This underlies the traditional Christian practice of facing east in prayer and worship.
primary_basis: Genesis 2:8; 3:24 — Eden is associated with the east, contributing to the symbolism of paradise and restored access to God.
Ezekiel 43:1–5 — the glory of the Lord enters the restored temple from the east.
Ezekiel 44:1–3 — the eastern gate is sanctified by the Lord’s entrance.
Matthew 24:27 — the coming of the Son of Man is compared to lightning shining from east to west.
Revelation 7:2 — an angel bearing the seal of the living God ascends from the rising of the sun.
Malachi 4:2 — the “sun of righteousness” rising with healing is often connected typologically with Christ and eastward orientation.

alternatives.meaning: Alienation from God, exile, or human rebellion: movement eastward or residence east of sacred space can mark departure from Eden and increasing estrangement.
basis: Genesis 3:24 — humanity is expelled from Eden, with cherubim stationed on its eastern side.
Genesis 4:16 — Cain settles east of Eden after judgment.
Genesis 11:1–9 — the movement associated with Babel is rendered as eastward or from the east, depending on translation.
Genesis 13:11 — Lot journeys eastward toward the cities of the plain.

alternatives.meaning: Judgment, destruction, or adversity, particularly through the biblical motif of the east wind.
basis: Exodus 10:13; 14:21 — an east wind brings the locust plague and divides the sea.
Job 27:21 — the east wind carries the wicked away.
Jeremiah 18:17 — God scatters his people like an east wind.
Hosea 13:15 — the east wind brings desolation.
Jonah 4:8 — a scorching east wind afflicts Jonah.

alternatives.meaning: The nations, peoples, wisdom, or riches located east of Israel rather than a fixed theological symbol.
basis: Genesis 29:1 — Jacob travels to the land of the peoples of the east.
1 Kings 4:30 — the wisdom of Solomon is compared with the wisdom of the people of the east.
Matthew 2:1–2 — the Magi come from the east seeking the newborn king.

alternatives.meaning: A sacred architectural direction associated with temple access, worship, and divine glory.
basis: Exodus 27:13–16 — the tabernacle court entrance is on the east side.
Numbers 3:38 — Moses, Aaron, and his sons camp before the tabernacle toward the east.
Ezekiel 40:6; 43:1–5 — the eastern gate features prominently in the visionary temple and the return of divine glory.

notes: There is no settled, context-independent biblical symbolism of “east.” Positive Christian and liturgical interpretation most often connects it with divine appearing, Christ’s return, resurrection, and paradise, but biblical narratives also use eastward movement and the east wind for exile, rebellion, or judgment. Meaning therefore depends strongly on the passage and whether the reference is directional, geographical, architectural, or meteorological.
